mainTopic: What is included in a sale: a bathhouse, an olive press, and a whole city (slaves, the סנטר, and בית השלחין)
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא: a plain sale of a בית המרחץ leaves out things like the wood storeroom, but 'and all its accompaniments' includes everything. In a real case, a man sold a בית הבד 'with all its accompaniments,' and there were stores outside it where sesame was dried. רב יוסף ruled from that ברייתא that the stores were sold. אביי challenged him from רבי חייא's ברייתא, which says not everything is sold. רב אשי decided that the stores are sold only if the seller also named boundaries that include them. Then a new משנה teaches that selling a city includes its fixed structures but not its מטלטלין, unless the seller says 'it and everything in it.' The גמרא tries to prove from this משנה that a slave counts as movable property, but רב אשי shows the proof fails. Last, the גמרא asks what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's word סנטר means, either the land registrar or the fields, and tests each view against the משנה's term בית השלחין in two versions. The second version's challenge to the registrar view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the teaching on selling a bathhouse
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its list of things not sold with a בית המרחץ, then says that if the seller adds 'and all its accompaniments,' everything is sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: [He did not sell what supplies the bathhouse] in the summer and in the rainy season, nor the wood storeroom. But if he said to him, 'I am selling you the bathhouse and all its accompaniments,' all of them are sold.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the last lines of a ברייתא about selling a בית המרחץ. It lists things that are not included, and then gives the wording that does include them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain sale of a בית המרחץ covers only the bathhouse itself, not things outside it like the wood storeroom. Adding the words 'and all its accompaniments' widens the sale so that everything is included. This exact line becomes the source רב יוסף uses in the next case.

keyTerms.meaning: Its accompaniments, the things used with it

phrases.english: in the summer season and in the rainy season,
phrases.notes: This is the tail end of a teaching that started on the previous page, about what is not included when selling a bathhouse.

phrases.english: nor the storeroom for the wood.
But if he said to him:
"The bathhouse and all of its accompaniments
I am selling to you" –
all of them are sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אָמַר לוֹ: בֵּית הַמֶּרְחָץ וְכׇל תַּשְׁמִישָׁיו אֲנִי מוֹכֵר לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A plain sale of a bathhouse leaves out outside items like the wood storeroom. Saying 'and all its accompaniments' includes them all.

steps.title: A real case: selling an olive press with its accompaniments
steps.stepSummary: A man sold a בית הבד 'and all its accompaniments.' There were stores outside it used for drying sesame, and the buyer brought the case to רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man said to his fellow, 'I am selling you the olive press and all its accompaniments.' There were some stores outside, where people would spread out sesame seeds. He came before רב יוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story and sets up a question. Were the outside stores included in the sale?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller used the same wide wording as the ברייתא: 'and all its accompaniments.' But the stores stood outside the press and were only partly used for it, for drying sesame. So it is unclear whether they count as part of the בית הבד.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to his fellow:
"The olive press and all of its accompaniments
I am selling to you."
There were certain stores outside,
where they would spread out sesame seeds in them.
He came before רב יוסף.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא's 'all its accompaniments' wording to a new real case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are stores outside the olive press, used for drying sesame, included in a sale of 'the olive press and all its accompaniments'?

steps.title: רב יוסף rules the stores were sold
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף cites the ברייתא: when one sells 'the bathhouse and all its accompaniments,' everything is sold. So here too the stores are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We learned: if he said, 'I am selling you the bathhouse and all its accompaniments,' all of them are sold.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the case by quoting the ברייתא from Step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He compares the בית הבד to the בית המרחץ. In both cases the seller said 'and all its accompaniments.' So just as the outside items of the bathhouse are sold, the outside stores of the olive press are sold too.

phrases.english: He said to him: We have learned:
If he said:
"The bathhouse and all of its accompaniments
I am selling to you" –
then all of them are sold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the case by citing the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The stores are sold, because the ברייתא says everything is sold when the seller adds 'and all its accompaniments.'

steps.title: אביי objects from רבי חייא's teaching
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that רבי חייא taught the opposite: not everything is sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But רבי חייא taught: they are not all sold!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's ruling with a different ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא's version says that even with the wide wording, not everything is sold. That undercuts רב יוסף's proof. Now we have two ברייתות that seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught? (a challenge from a teaching)
Not all of them are sold

phrases.english: אביי said to him:
But didn't רבי חייא teach:
Not all of them are sold!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's ruling that the stores were sold, based on the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא, taught by רבי חייא, says not everything is sold even with that wording, so the proof does not hold.

steps.title: רב אשי: it depends on whether boundaries were stated
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rules that the buyer gets the stores only if the seller also said 'and these are its boundaries.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: We look. If he said to him, 'the olive press and all its accompaniments, and these are its boundaries,' he acquires. If not, he does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the final way to settle the case and resolves the clash between the two teachings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'All its accompaniments' alone is not enough to include outside property like the stores. But if the seller also named boundaries that take in the stores, they are part of the sale. This explains how one teaching can say 'all are sold' and the other 'not all are sold.'
steps.whatToRemember: Saying 'and all its accompaniments' does not by itself include outside property. Naming the boundaries does.

phrases.english: Rather, רב אשי said:
We look:
If he said to him:
"The olive press and all of its accompaniments,
and these are its boundaries" –
phrases.notes: He means boundaries that take in the area of the outside stores.

phrases.english: he acquires them;
and if not, he does not acquire them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves אביי's challenge and decides the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'All its accompaniments' alone includes even outside stores (רב יוסף).
steps.terutzMaskana: The outside stores are included only if the seller also stated boundaries that cover them.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Outside property belongs to the buyer only if the seller named boundaries that include it.

steps.title: New משנה: what is included when selling a city
steps.stepSummary: Selling a city includes its houses, pits, ditches, caves, bathhouses, dovecotes, olive presses and בית השלחין, but not its מטלטלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who sells a city has sold the houses; the pits, ditches and caves; the bathhouses and dovecotes; the olive presses and the בית השלחין; but not the movable property.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with the basic rule for selling an entire city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything fixed to the ground in the city is part of the sale. Things that can be moved around, called מטלטלין, are not included in a plain sale.

keyTerms.meaning: A term the גמרא will explain

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who sells the city –
has sold the houses;
the pits, ditches and caves;
the bathhouses and dovecotes;
the olive presses and the beit hashelachin;
but not the movable property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sale of a city includes its fixed structures but not its movable property.

steps.title: Selling the city 'and everything in it'
steps.stepSummary: If the seller says 'it and everything in it,' even animals and slaves in the city are sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: But when he said to him, 'it and everything in it,' even if there were animals and slaves in it, all of them are sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds wording that changes the result of the basic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'and everything in it' widens the sale beyond the fixed structures. Even movable things such as animals and slaves are now included.

phrases.english: But when he said to him:
"It and everything that is in it" –
even if there were animals and slaves in it,
all of them are sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ: הִיא וְכׇל מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a wording that widens the basic rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'It and everything in it' includes even animals and slaves.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: the סנטר is sold with the city
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that selling a city also includes the סנטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: One who sells the city has sold the סנטר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds one more thing that comes with the sale of a city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not explain what the סנטר is. The גמרא defines it in step 13. For now, just note that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל includes it in a plain sale of the city.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, נשיא of the סנהדרין
A term the גמרא will explain

steps.whatToRemember: A plain sale of a city covers its fixed structures. 'And everything in it' adds even movables. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds the סנטר.

phrases.english: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:
One who sells the city –
has sold the santar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further item to the sale of a city.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Selling a city includes the סנטר.

steps.title: Trying to prove a slave is like movable property
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב אויא tells רב אשי that the משנה proves a slave is treated like movable property, because slaves are not automatically sold with the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב אחא בריה דרב אויא said to רב אשי: Learn from this that a slave is like movable property. If a slave were like land, he should be sold automatically along with the city!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by trying to learn a general rule from the משנה. The rule is that an עבד כנעני counts as מטלטלין, not as קרקע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Houses and pits are land, and the משנה says they are sold automatically with the city. Slaves are only sold if the seller says 'it and everything in it.' So רב אחא reasons that slaves must not be like land, or they would go along with the city just like the houses do.

phrases.english: GEMARA

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַוְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rav Avya said to Rav Ashi:
Learn from it
phrases.notes: 'It' is the משנה, which says slaves are only sold if the seller says 'it and everything in it.'

phrases.english: a slave is like movable property;
for if he were like land,
he should be sold along with the city!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule about slaves from the משנה's ruling in steps 6-7.
steps.raayaObject: That an עבד has the status of מטלטלין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה says slaves are not sold automatically with a city, while the city's land is.

steps.title: Counter-challenge: then why does the משנה say 'even'?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks back: if a slave is movable property, why does the משנה need the word 'even' about slaves?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי replied: But what, then? Are you saying a slave is like movable property? If so, why does the משנה say 'even'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי turns the argument around and challenges רב אחא's proof. He points to the word אפילו in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if the seller said 'it and everything in it,' then even animals and slaves are sold. If slaves were plain movable property, they would obviously be included with everything else, and the word 'even' would add nothing. So the משנה's wording seems to treat slaves as something more than ordinary movables.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather, what [do you want to say]?

phrases.english: But rather, what [are you saying],
a slave is like movable property?!
Then what is the meaning of 'even'?
phrases.notes: He's pointing at the משנה's words: 'even animals and slaves' are sold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof from step 9 by using the משנה's own wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא's claim that a slave is like movable property
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If slaves were ordinary movables, the word 'even' would be pointless, since they would naturally be included in 'everything in it.'

steps.title: Movable or land, a self-moving slave is different
steps.stepSummary: Both views must say that a slave, because he moves on his own, is a special type, so the משנה proves nothing either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must you say? There is a difference between movable property that moves on its own and movable property that does not. In the same way, even if you say a slave is like land, there is a difference between land that moves on its own and land that does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes knocking down the proof. He shows that each side needs the same distinction, so the משנה cannot decide the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To explain the word 'even,' רב אחא must admit that slaves are a special kind of movable property because they walk around. But then someone who says slaves are like land can use the same idea: slaves are a special kind of land that walks away, so they are not sold automatically with the city. Since both readings fit the משנה, there is no proof.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives no proof about a slave's status. Whether he is like land or like movables, his ability to move on his own puts him in a special group.

phrases.english: Rather, what do you have to say?
There is a difference between movable property that moves on its own
and movable property that does not move;
even if you say a slave is like land,
there is a difference between land that moves on its own
and land that does not move.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the distinction that step 10 forced on רב אחא to show that the proof in step 9 fails.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole proof from step 9
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'self-moving' distinction explains the משנה equally well whether a slave is like land or like movables.

steps.title: What does סנטר mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's statement and asks what the word סנטר means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: One who sells a city has sold the סנטר. What is the סנטר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה. It quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's words so it can ask about the unusual word סנטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 already gave רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling. Here the גמרא repeats it only to define the hard word in it. The answer will decide what extra thing he thinks goes along with a city sale.

keyTerms.meaning: An unclear word; the גמרא is about to define it

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת הָעִיר – מָכַר אֶת הַסַּנְטֵר.
phrases.english: One who sells the city has sold the santar.
What is the 'santar'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה (step 8) to define a key word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word סנטר

steps.title: Two meanings: land registrar or fields
steps.stepSummary: In בבל they explained סנטר as the land registrar, and שמעון בן אבטולמוס says it means the fields around the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here they explained it as the land registrar. שמעון בן אבטולמוס says: the fields.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two different definitions of סנטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One view says סנטר is a person: the official who keeps track of property boundaries (בר מחווניתא). The other view says it is land: the fields that surround the city (באגי).

keyTerms.meaning: The land registrar who keeps track of boundaries

phrases.english: Here they explained it as the land registrar.
Shimon ben Avtolemos says: the fields.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סנטר is either the land registrar (בר מחווניתא) or the surrounding fields (באגי).

steps.title: What each definition means in practice
steps.stepSummary: If סנטר is the registrar, the fields are surely sold too. If סנטר is the fields, the registrar is not sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says it is the land registrar holds that the fields are all the more so sold. The one who says it is the fields holds that the registrar is not sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how far each view goes. It shows exactly what is sold with the city according to each definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The registrar is less connected to the city than its fields. So if רבן שמעון בן גמליאל includes even the registrar, he surely includes the fields. But if סנטר only means the fields, then the registrar stays out of the sale.

phrases.english: The one who says it is the land registrar:
all the more so the fields [are sold];
the one who says it is the fields:
but the land registrar is not sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר בַּר מַחְווֹנִיתָא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן בָּאגֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out what follows in practice from each definition in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Registrar view: both the registrar and the fields are sold. Fields view: only the fields are sold, not the registrar.

steps.title: Setting up a proof from בית השלחין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה lists בית השלחין as sold with the city and assumes שלחין means fields, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: the olive presses and the בית השלחין. They assumed: what is שלחין? Fields, as it is written: 'And sends water upon the fields.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It brings words from the משנה and gives them a meaning that it will soon use to test the two views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא of the משנה already lists בית השלחין among the things sold with a city. At first the גמרא assumes שלחין means fields, because the פסוק uses the word שולח (sends) for watering fields. If so, the תנא קמא already says that fields are sold.
steps.confusionAlert: סברוה means this is only a first assumption. In step 17 the גמרא rejects this meaning of שלחין.

phrases.english: We learned: the olive presses and the beit hashelachin.
They assumed: what is 'shelachin'? Fields,
as it is written: 'And sends water upon the fields';

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a line from the משנה (step 6) to test the two definitions of סנטר from steps 13-14.
steps.raayaObject: Which definition of סנטר is correct
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's listing of בית השלחין, read as fields using איוב 5:10

steps.title: The 'fields' view makes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל say nothing new
steps.stepSummary: If סנטר means fields, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would be repeating the תנא קמא, who already said fields are sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted according to the one who says it is the land registrar: the תנא קמא said the fields are sold but the registrar is not, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל comes to say that even the registrar is sold. But according to the one who says it is the fields, the תנא קמא also says this!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the view that סנטר means fields. On that view, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would not be adding anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The registrar view fits well: the תנא קמא sold only the fields (בית השלחין), and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds the registrar. But if סנטר means fields, the תנא קמא already said fields are sold. Then there is no disagreement and nothing new in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's words.

keyTerms.meaning: The first (anonymous) תנא of the משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: A תנא who disagrees in a משנה is expected to add something new. If one definition makes him repeat the תנא קמא, that definition is in trouble.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says it is the land registrar,
the first tanna said: the fields are sold,
the land registrar is not sold;

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲתָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לְמֵימַר:
phrases.english: and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel comes to say:
even the land registrar is also sold.
But according to the one who says it is the fields,
the first tanna says this too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reading of בית השלחין from step 15 to attack the 'fields' definition from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמעון בן אבטולמוס's definition of סנטר as fields
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תנא קמא already includes fields (בית השלחין), so on this view רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would add nothing and would not be disagreeing.

steps.title: שלחין means gardens, not fields
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the assumption that שלחין means fields. It means gardens inside the city, as the פסוק shows. So according to the תנא קמא, the fields are not sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think שלחין means fields? No. שלחין means gardens, as the פסוק says: 'Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates.' But the fields are not sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 16. It shows that the word שלחין in the משנה was misunderstood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the תנא קמא already said fields are sold, because שלחין meant fields. Now the גמרא says שלחין means gardens, based on a פסוק in שיר השירים. That means the תנא קמא only said gardens are sold, and the fields outside the city are not.

keyTerms.meaning: In this answer: gardens inside the city
Do you think...? (a way of rejecting an assumption)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two words. סנטר is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's word, and שלחין is the תנא קמא's word. This step only changes how we read שלחין.

phrases.english: Do you think that what שלחין means is fields?!
phrases.notes: This is the assumption from step 15, which the גמרא is now throwing out.

phrases.english: No; what does שלחין mean? Gardens,
as it says: 'Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates';
but fields are not sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ מַאי שְׁלָחִין בָּאגֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 by rejecting the assumption made in step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שלחין means fields, so the תנא קמא already said fields are sold.
steps.terutzMaskana: שלחין means gardens, so according to the תנא קמא the fields are not sold.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that fields are sold too
steps.stepSummary: Now רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is not repeating the תנא קמא. He is adding that even the fields are sold, so reading סנטר as fields works.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבן שמעון בן גמליאל comes to say that even the fields are sold too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer and closes the first version of the discussion. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is saying something new after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא sold only the gardens. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees and adds the fields as well. So the opinion that סנטר means fields no longer makes him repeat the תנא קמא.

keyTerms.meaning: And he comes to say (he is adding something new)

steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, the תנא קמא sells the city's gardens but not its fields. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds the fields. That is why סנטר can mean fields.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲתָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לְמֵימַר:
phrases.english: And רבן שמעון בן גמליאל comes to say:
even fields are also sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲתָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from step 17 by showing what new point רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Reading סנטר as fields is fine, because רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds fields to the תנא קמא's gardens.

steps.title: A second version begins, assuming שלחין means gardens
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא presents another version of the discussion. Here, from the start, they assume שלחין means gardens.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the discussion went like this: they assumed that שלחין means gardens.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second version of the whole discussion. This line sets up the starting assumption for that version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the conclusion 'gardens' came only as an answer to a challenge. In this version, 'gardens' is the starting point. That will change which opinion about סנטר runs into trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (another version of the discussion)

phrases.english: Some say: they assumed,
what does שלחין mean? Gardens;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a different version of steps 15 to 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, שלחין is assumed from the start to mean gardens.

steps.title: The opinion that סנטר means fields works well
steps.stepSummary: Using בשלמא, the גמרא shows that the opinion that סנטר means fields fits well. The תנא קמא sells gardens but not fields, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds the fields. This sets up a challenge against the other opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says סנטר means fields: the תנא קמא said gardens are sold but fields are not, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל comes to say that even fields are sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. First it shows which opinion fits easily, so it can then challenge the opinion that סנטר means the registrar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בשלמא means 'it's fine for this view.' If שלחין is gardens and סנטר is fields, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל clearly adds something new. The question still coming is how the registrar opinion explains רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: It is fine, it makes sense (for one view, before a 'but' about the other view)
According to the one who says
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: בשלמא is not the end of the argument. It always prepares for a challenge against the other side. Here that challenge, against the opinion that סנטר means the registrar, comes at the start of the next amud.

phrases.english: It makes sense according to the one who says fields:
phrases.notes: He means the one who explains סנטר as the fields around the city.

phrases.english: the first opinion said:
gardens are sold,
fields are not sold;

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲתָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לְמֵימַר:
phrases.english: and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל comes to say:
even fields are sold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the assumption of step 19 to show that the 'fields' opinion fits, preparing a challenge to the 'registrar' opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If שלחין means gardens, the view that סנטר means fields gives רבן שמעון בן גמליאל a new point: he adds the fields.
